items.tx:
I read JD Vance's post on this site yesterday and at first I was shocked. The Vice President all but admitted that his own administration made a mistake going to war with Iran. I can't think of a sitting VP breaking with his President this publicly in my lifetime.

And at first glance his analysis seems spot on. His first prescription is to end the war. A war that he and the President, until this week, refused to even call a war.

It's hard to disagree with him. But like everything MAGA, the thread of truth is there to hide the larger truth. And the larger truth is this.

Tuesday was the greatest repudiation of a sitting President by voters in the history of this country. 

Not a repudiation of a policy. A repudiation of a man.

The message was not only about Iran or Israel or slogans or even the price at the pump. The message was simple.

WE ARE DONE WITH DONALD TRUMP.

We are done with his lies. We are done with the corruption and the gaslighting. We are done with the insanity. We are done with the cruelty.

The message from Mississippi to Iowa, from Kansas to Maine, from North Carolina to Texas, young and old, North and South, East and West, was the same.

Fuck Donald Trump.

This country desperately needs a healthy Republican Party. A party with room for Mitt Romney and Thomas Massie, for Chris Christie and (I can't believe I'm saying this) Marjorie Taylor Greene. A party that puts this constitutional republic above the interests of one man. A party that knows the difference between a Ken Paxton and a John Cornyn, between a Vivek Ramaswamy and a Mike DeWine.

That is the message voters sent on Tuesday, with more ballots cast than in any midterm in American history. 

WE ARE DONE WITH DONALD TRUMP. 

The sooner the brave members of whatever remains of the Republican Party understand that, the sooner we can begin to heal.

I hope Democrats in Congress heard it too. Voters sent the same message in 2020, and we failed to make it stick. I for one don't think this country can afford 26 more months of this madness before we do the one thing voters just demanded in historic numbers.

Trump needs to leave, and he needs to leave now.

All it would take this January is eleven Republican senators willing to acknowledge the existential threat this lawless President poses to the country and the world. Eleven brave Republicans need to stand up and end this madness. Save their party. Save the country.

It's up to all of us to give them the courage to do what's right.

President Trump today advanced an important discussion with several European leaders about the need for a broader European security architecture that can help establish the conditions for lasting peace.

Building on his leadership and the substantive work undertaken this week in Brussels with Ukraine, NATO, and our European partners, @SEPeaceMissions and I wanted to share some of the objectives guiding our ongoing discussions.

For more than 30 years, Europe and Russia have struggled to establish a sustainable security framework. Decades of mistrust, competing security concerns, and the devastating consequences of this war make this an extraordinarily difficult challenge, but one that is essential to lasting peace.

Our objective is to develop practical arrangements that address the security concerns of all sides, reduce the risk of future conflict, and create a more stable and predictable security environment.

We are exploring five principal goals: permanent security consultations, reliable crisis communications, greater military transparency, reciprocal measures to reduce escalation risks, and an enduring framework for long-term European security and stability.

Any arrangements must fully respect the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and independent decision-making of every nation. Each country will retain authority over its own security and alliances, and no country would have a veto over another’s sovereign choices. NATO will remain central to European collective defense, and this initiative would build upon existing institutions and commitments.

We will continue consultations through the Shell Bay format with Ukraine, NATO, the EU, and our European partners, expanding engagement to ensure that all relevant perspectives and ideas are considered. We will also engage Russia as part of the peace negotiations.

Next week in Abu Dhabi, the United States will convene the first trilateral peace discussions with Ukraine and Russia since February. All parties remain intensely engaged in preparing for substantive and productive negotiations. We will consult closely with our European partners on the sidelines and, if progress is made, aim to move toward a broader multilateral format with their direct participation.

These ideas continue to evolve, and we welcome thoughtful input. Creating the right structure will be critical to ending this war and transitioning from conflict toward conditions that make possible a durable peace.

This is difficult, detailed work. There are no easy solutions. But the opportunity to help end this devastating war and build a foundation for a more peaceful, secure, and prosperous Europe for generations to come makes it a challenge well worth undertaking.

We will see how these discussions develop and continue working intensively with all parties toward President Trump’s objective of a comprehensive and lasting peace.

 “Let’s be realistic. One day, the United States will elect a president who does not like Israel. It could happen in two years, six years, or ten years.”

Dermer explains that Israel can still work with such a president.

Because one day, the CIA Director will walk into the Oval Office and say:

An anti-American president sitting in the Oval Office.”

Why does he speak about Israel’s economic independence? Why does he seek to reduce dependence on American aid? Why does he believe Israel must be capable of securing its own future?

Because no one can guarantee who will be sitting in the White House a few years from now.

The less Israel depends on political changes in Washington, the stronger the alliance between the two countries can become.

Historic midterm victories are sparking celebrations among voters from communities long underrepresented in American politics.
